Kuvitus: muuttopäivä kerrostalon pihalla: Illustration: moving day in the yard of an apartment building. The rear doors of a van are open, and a wooden loading ramp slopes down from the floor of the van to the ground. In the middle of the ramp there is a cardboard moving box that stays in place. Inside the van there are more boxes, and a mover is carrying one box beside the ramp. In a small picture in the sky a steeper ramp, on which the box slides down, and a blue arrow shows the direction of motion.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: vaaka-akselilla l: Graph to scale: on the horizontal axis the horizontal force F pulling the box in newtons from zero to 80, on the vertical axis the friction force of the floor in newtons from zero to 60. A normal force of 100 newtons presses the box against the floor. At first the friction force grows equal to the pull: a straight line rises from the origin to the point where the pull and the friction are 50 newtons. This is the greatest value of static friction, mu zero times N. There the box starts to move, and the friction force drops along a dashed line to 35 newtons, mu times N, and stays there as the pull grows.
Kaksi kuvaa. Vasemmalla tilannekuva: avo: Two pictures. On the left a snapshot: a pickup truck starts moving to the right and accelerates, and on its bed there is a box that does not slide on the bed. Above the box a thin orange arrow a points to the right. On the right the free-body diagram of the box as a rectangle: the weight G from the center down, the normal force N of the bed from the lower surface up and as long as the weight, and the friction force of the bed from the front corner of the lower surface to the right, that is in the direction of motion. The friction force is much shorter than the weight.
Kaksi kuvaa. Vasemmalla tilannekuva: laa: Two pictures. On the left a snapshot: a box is at rest on a wooden plank that rises to the right at an angle alpha to the horizontal. On the right the free-body diagram of the box, the box tilted as a rectangle like on the plank: the weight G from the center straight down, the normal force N from the lower surface perpendicular to the surface, outward, and the static friction from the upper corner of the lower surface parallel to the surface, up the slope. The components of the weight are drawn dashed from the center: G x down the slope and G y perpendicular to the surface, toward it. The angle between the weight and the component G y is alpha. The component G y is as long as the normal force and G x as long as the friction force.
Laatikon voimakuvio, laatikko suorakulmi: Free-body diagram of a box, the box as a rectangle tilted along a 25 degree slope. The weight G from the center straight down. The normal force N from the lower surface perpendicular to the surface, outward. The kinetic friction from the upper corner of the lower surface up the slope, because the box slides down. The components of the weight dashed from the center: G x down the slope and G y perpendicular to the surface, toward it. G x is longer than the friction force. Separately a thin orange acceleration arrow a down the slope. In the corner the axes: x down the slope and y perpendicular to the surface, outward.
Opiskelijan piirtämä voimakuvio rinnettä: A free-body diagram drawn by a student of a box sliding down a slope, the box as a rectangle tilted along the slope. From the center an arrow G straight down. From the lower surface an arrow N straight up, vertical. From the upper corner of the lower surface an arrow parallel to the slope, up the slope.
Laatikon voimakuvio, laatikko suorakulmi: Free-body diagram of a box, the box as a rectangle tilted along the slope. The weight G from the center straight down, the normal force N from the lower surface perpendicular to the surface, outward, and the friction force from the upper corner of the lower surface up the slope.

Free-body diagram of a box, the box as a rectangle tilted along the slope. The weight G from the center straight down, the normal force N from the lower surface perpendicular to the surface, outward, and the friction force from the lower corner of the lower surface down the slope.

Free-body diagram of a box, the box as a rectangle tilted along the slope. The weight G from the center straight down and the normal force N from the lower surface perpendicular to the surface, outward. There are no other arrows.

Free-body diagram of a box, the box as a rectangle tilted along the slope. The weight G from the center perpendicular to the slope, toward it, the normal force N from the lower surface perpendicular to the surface, outward, and the friction force from the upper corner of the lower surface up the slope.
Mallikuvio: laatikkoa vedetään köydellä: Model diagram: a box is pulled up a slope by a rope at a constant velocity, the rope parallel to the slope. The diagram has only the box, as a rectangle tilted along the slope. The weight G from the center straight down. The normal force N from the lower surface perpendicular to the surface, outward. The tension T of the rope from the middle of the upper side up the slope. The kinetic friction from the lower corner of the lower surface down the slope, because the box slides up. The components of the weight dashed. Separately a thin blue velocity arrow v up the slope. In the corner the axes: x up the slope and y perpendicular to the surface, outward.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa, esimerkkiaineisto: Graph to scale, example data. On the horizontal axis the normal force N in newtons from zero to 30, on the vertical axis the friction force in newtons from zero to 7. Five measurement points: at a normal force of 5 newtons the friction force is 1.1 newtons, at 10 newtons 2.1, at 15 newtons 3.3, at 20 newtons 4.2 and at 25 newtons 5.4 newtons. The line has not been drawn.
